detail.title: Трансдисциплинарные исследования в публичном управлении: проблема концептуально-методологических оснований (Transdisciplinary Research in Public Administration: The Problem of Conceptual and Methodological Foundations)
detail.abstract:
Russian Abstract: Трансдисциплинарные исследования сегодня активно приме- няются в самых различных областях, в том числе в области публичного управления для решения важнейших проблем общественной жизни. По определению, трансдисциплинар- ные исследования призваны преодолевать дисциплинарные барьеры, а также привлекать к исследованиям специалистов-практиков и широкую общественность с целью получения новых идей, знаний, решений. Существует широкое разноо- бразие проводимых сегодня исследований, которые характе- ризуют как трансдисциплинарные. При этом концептуальные и методологические основы таких исследований остаются не- достаточно проясненными. В статье рассматриваются такие вопросы, как разновидности трансдисциплинарных исследова- ний, уровни достижения трансдисциплинарного видения реша- емых проблем, а также проблема участия непрофессионалов для создания новых знаний. Для развития данных исследова- ний требуется дальнейшая разработка концептуальных и мето- дологических основ трансдисциплинарности.

English Abstract: Transdisciplinary research is currently being actively applied in a wide variety of fields, including public administration, to address the most pressing issues in society. By definition, transdisciplinary research aims to overcome disciplinary barriers and engage practitioners and the public in order to generate new ideas, knowledge, and solutions. There is a wide variety of research being conducted today that is characterized as transdisciplinary. However, the conceptual and methodological foundations of such research remain insufficiently clarified. The article discusses issues such as the kinds of transdisciplinary research, the levels of achieving a transdisciplinary vision of the problems being solved, and the issue of involving non-professionals in creating new knowledge. Further development of the conceptual and methodological foundations of transdisciplinarity is required to advance such research.

title: Towards the Development of Detection of Learned Helplessness in Mathematics: Design and Data Collection Challenges from a Developing Country Perspective
affiliations: , University of the East, Don Honorio Ventura State University, Don Honorio Ventura State University, Don Honorio Ventura State University, Don Honorio Ventura State University, National University Philippines and Don Honorio Ventura State University

detail.title: Towards the Development of Detection of Learned Helplessness in Mathematics: Design and Data Collection Challenges from a Developing Country Perspective
detail.abstract: This study investigates the challenges in designing, data collection, and implementation of a web-based Tutoring System (TS) for teaching linear equations within a developing country context. Originally designed as an Android app, the system was redeveloped as a web application to facilitate cross-platform access and data collection. This redesign enabled enhanced tracking through interaction logs and included features like problem skipping, hints, difficulty-based problem sequencing, and game modes with adaptable progression (e.g., easy-to-hard, hard-toeasy). The main objective was to document the design and data collection challenges encountered in data collection for the development of a model capable of detecting learned helplessness in students' behaviors while using a web application for solving linear equation. Challenges included outdated devices, unreliable internet, and logistical constraints such as limited session durations and delays in obtaining approvals. Environmental disruptions like class cancellations and curriculum gaps further complicated the process, with only 118 out of 410 students eligible and actively participating. These obstacles highlight the complexities of collecting interaction data for detecting learned helplessness in real-world, resourceconstrained educational settings.

detail.abstract: We measure the effect of monetary policy announcements on mortgage-backed security (MBS) prices using trade-level data. High-frequency changes to MBS prices in the forward to-be-announced (TBA) market are highly correlated with 10-year Treasury yield surprises from Bauer and Swanson (2023). Additionally, surprise changes to implied financing rates from dollar roll transactions are highly correlated with high-frequency changes to repurchase agreement (repo) rates. Variation in price changes by coupon allows us to estimate discount, duration, and prepayment effects. The existence of distinguishable prepayment effects suggests that investors quickly incorporate expectations of prepayment behavior for the millions of households with callable mortgages. Finally, we show MBS surprises are more predictive of future mortgage rates than existing monetary policy surprise measures. The new measures are embedded within this PDF document.

title: Technical Foundations of the Reallocation Asset-Pricing Model

detail.title: Technical Foundations of the Reallocation Asset-Pricing Model

contentFormat.other: Technical Notes for The Reallocation Asset-Pricing Model

detail.abstract: This note develops the technical foundations of the Reallocation Asset-Pricing Model (RAM). It derives the continuous-time investor problem, the HJB equation, the stochastic discount factor, and the no-arbitrage martingale representation implied by reallocation-driven price dynamics. Market clearing endogenously determines the price of reallocation risk. The note also provides a microfoundation for the reallocation loading based on linear price impact, heterogeneous execution times, and flow-driven order arrival. These derivations formalize the RAM equilibrium underlying the main paper and clarify how path-dependent price adjustment generates a single priced factor associated with aggregate reallocation intensity. Lastly, it provides the equilibrium structure for the Consumption-Reallocation Asset-Pricing Model (CRAM)

publicationDetails.detailsText: Russian Journal of Church History, volume 6, issue 3, 2025[10.15829/2686-973X-2025-200]

detail.abstract: This article investigates the historical practice of fire insurance for immovable property organised by the Russian Orthodox Church on principles of reciprocity during the pre-revolutionary period. This subject remains underexplored in Russian historiography and merits closer examination. Focusing on the Kadnikov district of the Vologda diocese between 1910 and 1917, the study draws on archival insurance documents and materials from the Vologda Diocesan Gazette. It considers the organisation of mutual insurance at the district level, methods for valuing church property, the calculation of insurance premiums, recorded fire incidents, and the relationship between contributions and compensation for losses. The author also analyses cases where compensatory funds were used to finance rebuilding efforts. The data enables a comparative assessment of insurance outcomes for parishes and monasteries in Kadnikov relative to other districts within the Vologda diocese and the wider Russian Empire. The study concludes that mutual insurance was less advantageous for Kadnikov's ecclesiastical institutions, as premiums significantly exceeded fire damage compensations during the period under review.

title: The Role of Trade Agreements in Countering Trade Sanctions: Evidence from Sectoral Data
affiliations: Florida International University (FIU) - Department of Economics

detail.title: The Role of Trade Agreements in Countering Trade Sanctions: Evidence from Sectoral Data
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the extent to which free trade agreements can mitigate the adverse effects of politically motivated trade sanctions. Using a structural gravity model augmented with a crucial interaction term, we analyze a comprehensive panel dataset covering bilateral trade in 9 sectors across 167 countries from 1966 to 2020. Our empirical analysis, which relies on the robust Pseudo-Poisson Maximum Likelihood (PPML) estimator, yields three clear findings. We confirm that sanctions significantly reduce trade, while free trade agreements are a powerful catalyst for it. The core contribution, however, is that the existence of a free trade agreement substantially weakens the negative impact of a trade sanction. This shock absorber effect is consistently positive and statistically significant across all sectors. By systematically quantifying this resilience channel, our study reframes free trade agreements not merely as tools for trade promotion but as critical instruments for geoeconomic security in an age of global uncertainty.

title: Farmers’ Willingness to Pay for Granulated Urine Fertilizer in Malawi: Evidence from Incentive-Compatible Auctions and Information Interventions

detail.title: Farmers’ Willingness to Pay for Granulated Urine Fertilizer in Malawi: Evidence from Incentive-Compatible Auctions and Information Interventions
detail.abstract: Smallholder farmers in Malawi face persistent constraints in accessing affordable nitrogen fertilizers, underscoring the need for locally produced and circular nutrient solutions. Granulated urine fertilizer has recently emerged as a promising alternative, yet empirical evidence on farmers’ valuation and adoption drivers remains limited. This study used an incentive-compatible Becker–DeGroot–Marschak auction with 262 farmers in southern Malawi, complemented by a randomized information treatment providing nutrient, safety, and production details to understand farmers’ willingness to pay for granulated urine fertilizer. The results shows that baseline awareness of granulated urine fertilizer was extremely low (1 percent), but willingness to experiment was remarkably high, with 97 percent expressing readiness to try the product. Farmers’ bids ranged from MWK 400 to MWK 10,000, with a mean willingness to pay of MWK 1,903 per kilogram. The demand curve exhibited strong price elasticity, showing that 65 percent of farmers were willing to pay MWK 1,000 or less, while only 38 percent were willing to pay MWK 2,500 or more. Regression results reveal an important distinction between information exposure and information uptake. The intention-to-treat models show no significant effect of information on willingness to pay, indicating that a single information session did not immediately shift farmers’ valuations. However, the instrumental variable estimates demonstrate that information becomes significant once actual information awareness is isolated, suggesting that valuation increases only when farmers internalize and understand the safety and nutrient content information. Education, gender, and age consistently and positively predicted willingness to pay, while social acceptability concerns significantly reduced valuation. Women offered bids approximately MWK 550 higher than men, each additional year of schooling increased bids by about MWK 70, and concerns about acceptability reduced bids by nearly MWK 170. Overall, granulated urine fertilizer is valued as a mid-range nutrient input, perceived as more reliable than compost manure yet substantially cheaper than inorganic fertilizer. These findings highlight the importance of pricing strategies in the MWK 1,500–2,000 range, gender-responsive and education-tailored extension support, and multi-stage sensitization strategies that go beyond one-off information sessions to ensure meaningful understanding of this emerging circular nutrient technology.

title: The Reallocation Asset-Pricing Model

detail.title: The Reallocation Asset-Pricing Model
detail.abstract: This paper develops the Reallocation Asset-pricing Model (RAM), a framework in which expected returns arise from the path by which prices incorporate information. Because investors adjust portfolios at different speeds, prices move gradually, creating a priced source of systematic risk, reallocation risk, measured by each asset's sensitivity to reallocation flows. The RAM yields a single-factor pricing relation and shows that anomalies, including size, value, momentum, and reversal, reflect differences in this sensitivity rather than separate risk factors or behavioral errors. The framework predicts cross-sectional returns, time variation in risk premia, and market predictability, offering a unified alternative to existing models.

detail.abstract: Objective: Hospital readmissions impose a significant financial burden on healthcare systems and represent a critical failure in patient care continuity. This study leverages a Business Intelligence (BI) framework to analyze 5,000 historical patient encounters, aiming to isolate the primary determinants of early readmission. Methods: The research utilized a de-identified dataset of hospital admissions. A Star Schema data architecture was constructed to normalize the data, and a custom DAX-based risk stratification algorithm was developed to segment patients based on the interplay between comorbidity scores and Length of Stay (LOS). Results: The analysis established a baseline readmission rate of 18.8%. However, patients categorized as "Premature Discharge" (High Comorbidity, LOS < 3 days) exhibited a significantly higher readmission rate of 20.1%. Most notably, patients with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) discharged under this high-risk protocol showed a critical failure rate of 27.0%. Conclusion: The findings suggest that administrative decisions regarding discharge timing are a more significant predictor of readmission than clinical complexity alone. The study proposes the deployment of a dynamic "Risk Heatmap" dashboard to enable case managers to identify and intervene with high-risk patients prior to discharge.

detail.abstract:
The factory for white-collar work now fits on a laptop. A professional with ChatGPT and basic workflow tools can execute end-to-end production pipelines that previously required teams, templates, and institutional infrastructure. That's not productivity. That's the means of production relocating from the firm to the worker.

When intelligence becomes a non-scarce input available at consumer prices, the economics change fast. Markets drift toward commodity dynamics. Traditional firm advantages—"we hire smart people," "we have tight processes"—stop differentiating. At the same time, new landlords emerge: platforms that own the models, firms that own the best data and graphs, aggregators that control access to demand, regulators who decide who gets to play in high-stakes domains. The result is platform feudalism layered on top of a soft communism of cognition.

This paper maps that hybrid economy through two frameworks: Marx's analysis of who owns capital, and microeconomic theories of perfect competition. The strategic implications are structural. Firms can no longer compete on intelligence; they compete on the Process Intelligence Graph they own, the agentic systems they design, and the trust and risk-bearing they provide. Workers now carry portable capital; their leverage depends on building their own graphs, reputation, and networks while navigating multiple landlords. Policy choices will determine whether abundance flows toward wages and public goods or concentrates as platform rents.

This is not a prediction of utopia or dystopia. It's an analysis of power being renegotiated in real time. The question isn't whether cognitive engines will change white-collar economics. They already have. The question is whether we design firms, careers, and policies that are honest about that, or cling to 20th-century models while the ground shifts underneath us.

title: TrueSkills: AI-Resistant Assessment Through Personalized Understanding Validation

detail.title: TrueSkills: AI-Resistant Assessment Through Personalized Understanding Validation
detail.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has fundamentally disrupted traditional assessment methodologies in higher education. Students can now utilize tools like ChatGPT to generate essays and answer examination questions within seconds, exposing a critical weakness in assessment practices that prioritize memorization over genuine understanding. This paper presents TrueSkills, a novel assessment platform designed to evaluate conceptual understanding rather than information recall. The system operates through a two-phase protocol: students first produce original written content about a topic, after which the system generates personalized questions derived specifically from each student's unique submission. Since every student receives different questions tied to their own work, GenAI tools theoretically become ineffective for circumventing assessment-they would require access to the specific content each student created. A functional prototype has been developed that can accommodate up to 100 concurrent students. The fundamental principle is straightforward: instead of posing generic questions that GenAI can readily answer, the system generates questions about each student's specific examples and logical reasoning. Limited preliminary testing demonstrates the technical feasibility of the approach. However, comprehensive empirical validation of effectiveness remains necessary before claims about educational impact can be substantiated.

title: Big Data Value Realization in Project Management: The VALORE-BD Framework

detail.title: Big Data Value Realization in Project Management: The VALORE-BD Framework
detail.abstract:
Enterprises are undergoing a new phase of data-driven transformation in which Big Data (BD) plays a strategic role in reshaping organizational structures and decision-making processes. The rapid evolution of enabling infrastructures and emerging technologies, often characterized by black-box opacity, reinforces the need to reconceptualize both management of BD projects (BDPs) and assessment of value generated. Although several frameworks exist, few provide a comprehensive perspective that encompasses value measurement mechanisms, adaptability, and validation. This study addresses these gaps by proposing the VALORE-BD framework, developed through integration of scientific sources and empirical evidence, and conceived as a comprehensive and dynamic model oriented toward the design and implementation of BDDS. A systematic literature review was conducted on BD frameworks addressing value creation, transformation, and measurement in BDPs. The review enabled a structured classification of models, identification of distinctive features. To extend these insights, an exploratory phase based on questionnaires to domain experts was conducted to examine issues highlighted by the SLR. 

The VALORE-BD framework emphasizes value orientation, monitoring and measurement, control and observation mechanisms, adaptability, and organizational strategies for federated data and knowledge management, aimed at enhancing availability and reuse of information resources. Results from an expert-based validation indicate its potential as a managerial tool for BDPs, fostering knowledge integration and supporting the strategic governance of data-driven initiatives.

title: Thinking Outside the Hub: The Changing Geography of Venture Capital

detail.title: Thinking Outside the Hub: The Changing Geography of Venture Capital
detail.abstract: This paper investigates the effect of reduced information acquisition costs, enabled by broadband internet access, on the geography of venture capital (VC) investments and startup firms. Entrepreneurial activity in the United States is concentrated in California, Massachusetts, and New York, potentially due to high levels of VC fundraising in these states. Historically, VC firms have relied on in-person interactions to evaluate and monitor startups, leading to strong local bias in their investment decisions. Understanding whether remote communication technologies can mitigate this bias is critical for policymakers seeking to foster entrepreneurship in capital-constrained regions. Using a novel dataset of VC investments, internet speeds, and economic outcomes from 2010 to 2020, we leverage the plausibly exogenous introduction of Google Fiber to identify the effect of improved internet speeds on the geography of venture capitalists’ portfolio companies. Through difference-in-difference analysis, we find that VCs located in regions that receive high-speed internet become significantly more likely to invest in distant companies, particularly those in early stages and non-technology industries. The rise in distant financing has broader economic implications for states. Using instrumental variable analysis, we establish a causal relationship between increased out-of-state VC investments and small business formation in the recipient state. We find that, on average, a doubling in the number of out-of-state VC investments leads to a 9% increase in small business births, while a doubling in the total amount of out-of-state VC funding results in a 2% increase. These effects are particularly pronounced in states with lower levels of VC fundraising, suggesting that remote investments can mitigate local financing constraints and reduce regional disparities in entrepreneurial outcomes. Whereas conventional policy tools like investment tax credits have limited impact on attracting VC funding, we find that policies aimed at reducing information barriers, such as "Dig Once" regulations that lower the cost of broadband deployment, can also foster entrepreneurial growth.

detail.abstract:
This project, "Harnessing Customer Loyalty to Maximize Profitability: An Analytical Approach," is aimed at meeting Theni Thaniyam's need for a systematic, data-based approach as a traditional food producer and wholesaler in Tamil Nadu. The company had difficulty segmenting its most profitable customers and products since marketing and loyalty initiatives were directed at all customers equally without segmentation. This led to ineffective use of resources, minimal cross-selling and upselling, and excessive use of intuition-based decision-making.

To bridge these lags, the research used a mix of descriptive and predictive research on one year of sales data drawn from Tally. Preparation and cleaning of data was done in Excel, with subsequent descriptive analysis to determine the top 20 customers and top 20 products. Regression analysis was used to analyze price and quantity sold relationship to see demand sensitivity. Besides this, time-series forecasting also predicted monthly sales patterns for a period of two years, whereas Power BI dashboards were designed to show KPIs, customer-product mapping, profitability, and sales forecasts in an interactive way.

The results indicated that the top 20 products and customers contributed almost 70–75 percent of the overall revenue, validating the Pareto principle. Customer-product mapping identified a number of untapped cross-selling opportunities, while regression analysis validated a positive correlation between sales quantity and total revenue. Forecasting also indicated that sales would remain on an upward trend, with seasonal highs recurring each year. Power BI dashboards simplified reporting and enhanced decision-making by enabling real-time, interactive insights.

The findings of this research are straightforward for Theni Thaniyam. They should build loyalty programs with a focus on high-value customers and high margin products, plan strategic pricing and consider cross-selling and upselling to those high-value customers. They can also improve their planning for operations leverage the insights from their forecasting, to prepare for changes regarding demand for their inventory and resources. In conclusion, this once again demonstrates the capacity of combining loyalty analysis, product profitability and outcome forecasting to change decision making, drive profits and sustain long-term customer relationships.

detail.abstract:
Social media platforms have become core infrastructures for how firms communicate with customers, orchestrate marketing campaigns, and coordinate organizational activities in a globalized, data-rich environment. Yet many organizations-especially in emerging marketsmaintain an active presence on social media without translating that presence into systematic, data-informed business processes that support performance and growth. Recent work on digital transformation in emerging-market SMEs shows that digital tools are often adopted under severe constraints of infrastructure, regulation, and digital skills, which limit their impact on firm capabilities and competitiveness (Rampaul, 2025). At the same time, debates on datadriven versus data-informed decision-making emphasize the need to balance quantitative metrics with qualitative judgment, experience, and organizational learning (Abac, 2024) 

This working paper revisits and reframes a qualitative case study of a Turkish IT firm to examine how social media is embedded in organizational behavior and business processes under conditions of globalization. Drawing on structured questionnaires and eight in-depth interviews with customers, IT support, and a marketing manager, the study adopts a hermeneutic, interpretive perspective. All textual data were coded and analyzed using MAXQDA, following a constant-comparative logic that traced how respondents described social media’s role in customer interaction, recruitment, and internal coordination. The analysis shows that social media is used intensively for communication, reputation building, and attracting talent, but the underlying decision logic remains largely experience-based: social media data are rarely integrated into formal analytics, performance dashboards, or structured decision routines. The paper contributes to research on social media, digital transformation, and organizational behavior by (1) documenting the gap between social media presence and process-level transformation in an emerging-market context, (2) articulating how tensions between datadriven and experience-based logics manifest in everyday organizational practices and business programs in marketing and sales (Abac, 2024), and (3) outlining a research agenda for embedding social media data and analytics into decision processes in ways that enhance both business performance and organizational learning, while acknowledging infrastructure and capability constraints typical of emerging markets (Rampaul, 2025).

detail.abstract: Globalization and artificial intelligence (AI) are transforming the competitive landscape in which firms operate, yet organizations differ markedly in how they respond to these twin pressures. While some firms integrate AI and data analytics into their core decision processes, others continue to rely primarily on traditional, experience-based managerial logics. This paper develops a conceptual framework explaining how globalization, AI adoption, and organizational decision logic jointly shape organizational behavior and, ultimately, business performance. Drawing on research in global strategy, organizational behavior, and digital transformation, the paper distinguishes between AI-enabled, data-driven decision logic and traditional, experience-based decision logic. It argues that under conditions of heightened global competition, firms that combine AI capabilities with a learning-oriented, analytically driven organizational culture are better positioned to detect market shifts, experiment with new strategic options, and adapt business models. By contrast, firms that adopt AI superficially, or that resist AI and cling to purely experiential logics, risk misinterpreting complex environments and reinforcing rigid behavioral patterns that undermine competitiveness. The proposed framework highlights organizational learning, innovation behavior, and analytical culture as key behavioral mechanisms mediating the relationship between AIenabled decision making and business performance. It also identifies managerial AI literacy and digital capabilities as critical contingencies that condition whether AI becomes a strategic asset or a source of confusion and resistance. The paper concludes by outlining a set of propositions and an agenda for empirical research on how globalization and AI reshape organizational decision logics, behaviors, and performance in different sectors and institutional contexts.

detail.abstract: Effective scenario generation is crucial for supply chain decision-making under uncertainty, as it directly influences the performance of stochastic models used in planning. However, the question of how to generate scenarios from empirical supply chain data that is typically high-dimensional, correlated, noisy, and limited is not addressed. If correlation is considered at all, existing literature typically focuses on small settings, assuming correlation structures to be known or straightforward to estimate. In this work, we introduce covariance shrinkage as a novel technique for scenario generation in supply chain planning with limited historical data. By leveraging this finance-rooted method, we facilitate highdimensional estimation of demand correlation, reducing reliance on assumptions about independence or perfect knowledge of demand relationships. We demonstrate the advantage of using covariance shrinkage on a sales and operations planning problem in a global electronics manufacturing real-world case study. Using out-of-sample evaluation for a two-stage stochastic program, we compare various shrinkage methods against two benchmarks. Our case study results show that covariance shrinkage improves profit, achieving up to a 12% increase in profit outperformance compared to uncorrelated sampling. Additionally, it reduces profit variability compared to using the sample covariance directly. This methodology offers a solution for improving data-driven decision-making in supply chain planning under uncertainty.

detail.abstract: Purpose - SMEs play a leading role in the development of an economy, employment, and innovation in both developed and emerging economies. Nevertheless, SMEs never have enough financing to expand and compete adequately with their significance or otherwise. The aim of the paper is to discuss the alignment of SME finance and corporate strategy, as well as how strategic financial planning can give rise to resilience, improved access to capital, and sustainable growth. Design/methodology/approach - The method of the research will be a literature review that will synthesise the knowledge of the empirical study, the policy framework, and the emerging financial innovations. To explore the connection between financial constraints, governance, technology interventions, such as blockchain and fintech, and strategic decisions in the case of SMEs, the review takes into account international and regional foundations. Results - The article concludes that despite the emergence of alternative fund mechanisms, there is still limited access to liquidity and gaps in systemic funding by SMEs. There is alignment of financial planning to long-term corporate objectives so that capital can be made more readily available, to deal with risk, and to make a company competitive. It is discovered that good governance, financial literacy, and new financing instruments are instrumental in facilitating the sustainable development of the SMEs. Future research ought to employ empirical and cross-country methods to establish the connection between governance, financial innovation, and policy reforms in facilitating the financing of SMEs. Practical implications- The findings suggest that to prepare contextualised financial aid, to prepare financial literacy, to assume that there are SMEs, to prepare personalised credit facilities, and owners of SMEs have to consider financial management when planning how to do it. Originality/value - The need in this study is to have a unified framework whereby finance is not just an operating tool, but a growth, sustenance and long-term competitiveness catalyst of the SMEs.

title: Geopolitical risk and corporate supply chain stability: Evidence from China

detail.title: Geopolitical risk and corporate supply chain stability: Evidence from China
detail.abstract: This study provides novel micro-level evidence on the relationship between geopolitical risk (GPR) and corporate supply chain stability, drawing on an unbalanced panel of all firms listed on the Shanghai and Shenzhen A-share markets from 2010 to 2023. We construct an original firm-specific metric of geopolitical exposure by estimating the sensitivity of individual stock returns to innovations in the global GPR factor within a Fama–French asset pricing framework, thereby capturing the extent to which equity valuations are systematically loaded on geopolitical uncertainty. Baseline estimations reveal a statistically and economically significant deterioration in supply chain stability attributable to heightened GPR, a result that remains robust to alternative outcome measures, clustering schemes, high-dimensional fixed effects, subsample analyses, and placebo tests. Mechanism analysis demonstrates that GPR operates primarily through increased capital immobilization in accounts receivable and payable, alongside exacerbated financing constraints. The destabilizing effect is disproportionately pronounced among firms in capital-intensive and highly concentrated industries, with lower market power, and limited R&D intensity. A nonlinear specification further indicates that at elevated levels, GPR can induce resilience-enhancing technological upgrading and strategic reconfiguration.

detail.abstract: This literature review examines how artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming the auditing profession by reshaping its methods, ethics, and educational demands. Drawing on more than thirty peer-reviewed studies and recent industry analyses, the paper identifies three central themes: (1) the transformation of auditing practices through automation and continuous assurance, (2) the evolving role of human judgment and behavioral adaptation in AI-assisted audits, and (3) the emergence of explainability and governance frameworks designed to ensure accountability in AI applications. The integration of AI technologies such as machine learning, natural language processing, and robotic process automation enables auditors to analyze entire data populations in real time, enhancing efficiency, accuracy, and fraud detection. However, the literature also highlights challenges, including algorithm aversion, overreliance on technology, and ethical risks tied to transparency and independence. Studies suggest that AI effectiveness depends on human oversight, professional skepticism, and ethical governance rather than on complete automation. Furthermore, the review discusses how explainable AI and ethics-based auditing frameworks can ensure fairness and auditability in AI systems. Ultimately, the research underscores that the future of auditing will depend on combining human expertise with technological precision, promoting a new standard of integrity, adaptability, and accountability across the profession.

detail.abstract: This study discusses that organizations increasingly depend on digital platforms for daily operations; the rise of cyber threats has created an urgent need for advanced security solutions. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a critical tool in enhancing cybersecurity by improving threat detection, automating incident responses, and predicting potential attacks before they occur. This paper explores how AI technologies—such as machine learning, natural language processing, behavioral analytics, and deep learning—strengthen cyber defense systems and protect company data, employees, and customers. It also examines the associated risks, including algorithmic bias, adversarial attacks, privacy concerns, and the misuse of deepfake technologies, which can undermine trust and security. The discussion highlights the importance of integrating human oversight with AI-driven systems to ensure accountability, ethical management, and resilience. Furthermore, emerging solutions such as explainable AI, quantum security, and resilient architectures are analyzed as strategies to mitigate AI-related cybersecurity risks. Overall, this study concludes that although AI introduces new challenges, its benefits in detecting, preventing, and responding to cyber threats outweigh the drawbacks when implemented responsibly and with continuous human supervision.

title: LLM-Augmented Quantitative Finance: A Simple but Rigorous Framework for Market Understanding and Forecasting

detail.title: LLM-Augmented Quantitative Finance: A Simple but Rigorous Framework for Market Understanding and Forecasting
detail.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate strong abilities in pattern extraction, semantic understanding, and cross-modal reasoning. However, their integration into quantitative finance remains largely exploratory. This paper proposes a simple, modular, and mathematically explicit framework that combines LLM-based market reasoning with traditional quantitative models. We formalize an LLM feature pipeline, define a hybrid predictor, and prove several basic properties: (i) in-sample risk reduction when augmenting linear models with LLM features, (ii) conditions under which LLM sentiment is incrementally informative in the sense of conditional expectation, and (iii) a simple mean-variance interpretation of LLM-based regime features. We also provide placeholders for empirical figures (to be generated in Python) and discuss practical considerations for deploying LLMs in trading and risk-management pipelines.

detail.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence is reshaping the foundations of corporate governance by transforming decision-making, accountability, and ethical oversight within organizations. Recent research points both to the opportunities and the risks associated with integrating AI into governance frameworks. On one hand, AI offers the ability to enhance board efficiency, improve predictive capabilities for risk and performance, and strengthen organizational transparency through data-driven insights. On the other hand, it challenges traditional oversight structures by introducing issues of autonomy, bias, and diffusion of responsibility, which complicate the assignment of accountability and the maintenance of trust. Corporations face a turning point where they must decide whether to govern AI as a tool or allow AI to govern decision-making. Empirical studies reveal that AI can significantly bolster fraud detection, sustainability reporting, and strategic decision-making—but only if combined with robust ethical frameworks and effective human supervision. Meanwhile, ethical and regulatory dimensions are moving to the forefront, with guidelines advocating for transparency, fairness, and human-centric control over AI systems. The body of literature converges on the conclusion that while AI has the potential to optimize governance, it simultaneously magnifies existing dilemmas and introduces new ones. A balanced approach integrating ethical principles, crosssector collaboration, and adaptive regulation is essential to guide the responsible evolution of AI in corporate governance.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping how firms create, deliver, and capture value, particularly in the domains of marketing, customer engagement, and strategic decision-making. For firms operating in emerging markets, AI offers a potential pathway to overcome information constraints, better understand heterogeneous customer segments, and compete with both local and global rivals (Furman & Seamans, 2018; Georgieff & Hyee, 2022). However, existing research on AI in these contexts remains fragmented. Macro-level studies typically emphasize productivity, growth, or trade indicators (Frank et al., 2019; Goldfarb & Trefler, 2018), while firm-level work often focuses on technical or operational efficiency and pays limited attention to marketing transformation, consumer-related outcomes, and international competitiveness. This paper addresses this gap by developing an integrative review and conceptual framework that links AI-based firm capabilities, AI-enabled marketing and consumer-related outcomes, and the international competitiveness of firms in emerging markets. Methodologically, we conduct an integrative literature review spanning digital transformation, marketing, consumer behavior, and international business, synthesizing insights from dispersed empirical and conceptual contributions (Aldoseri et al., 2024; Dakalbab et al., 2024; Şova et al., 2024). The framework advances the argument that AI capabilitiessuch as advanced analytics, automation, and personalization-enhance customer insight, enable finer segmentation, and improve customer experience (Soni et al., 2019; Wang et al., 2024), which in turn support firms' performance in foreign markets and strengthen their competitive positioning. We further highlight the moderating role of contextual conditions in emerging markets, including digital infrastructure, human capital, institutional quality, and data governance (Gwagwa et al., 2021; Veale et al., 2023), in shaping the extent to which firms can effectively leverage AI. The paper concludes with implications for theory development in management and marketing, strategic and managerial guidance for firms deploying AI in domestic and international markets, and policy implications for fostering more competitive and inclusive digital business environments in emerging markets.

detail.title: Factors influencing implementation decisions in health care: A discrete choice experiment of intervention adoption
detail.abstract: BackgroundTo overcome barriers to the implementation of effective interventions, it is important to understand the factors which may influence stakeholders’ implementation decisions. We aimed to identify these factors and quantify their relative importance in the decision-making process. Stakeholders included those wishing to implement an intervention (e.g., health service researchers and providers), and those funding implementation efforts (e.g., administrators and policymakers).DesignWe utilized discrete choice experiment methodology to explore several factors relevant to implementation decisions. The survey instrument was developed through a systematic review and expert consultation process. Conditional and mixed logit models were used to capture observed and unobserved preference heterogeneity. We tested the robustness of our results with subgroup and sensitivity analyses.ResultsWe received 131 survey responses. There was a strong preference for intervention factors that 1) met stakeholders’ needs, 2) had excellent levels of evidence, and 3) demonstrated strong organizational readiness. An implementation cost of $150,000 was preferred by respondents over a lower cost of $100,000. This suggests that respondents may prioritize the other three factors over the cost of implementation. These results remained relatively consistent across professional subgroups and sensitivity analyses.ConclusionsMeeting stakeholders’ needs, levels of evidence, and organizational readiness had a large influence on implementation decisions. These factors were ranked of higher importance than implementation costs, administrative processes, and the presence of local champions within an organization. Designing research programs that support these influential factors will encourage successful implementation and ensure optimal healthcare delivery.

detail.abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) become increasingly integrated into high-stakes, human-facing applications, the need for rigorous auditing has grown. This paper examines the evolving landscape of LLM auditing, highlighting both the challenges and opportunities it presents. Key risks include algorithmic bias, privacy vulnerabilities, data provenance concerns, and accountability gaps, which traditional auditing approaches are often ill-equipped to address. The paper reviews emerging methodologies for auditing LLMs, including technical, ethical, and governance-focused approaches, emphasizing the importance of model explainability, data quality, and robust oversight frameworks. title: Limitations of Maximizing Shareholder Value in the Era of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
affiliations: Clarkson University - School of Business

detail.title: Limitations of Maximizing Shareholder Value in the Era of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
detail.abstract: The increasing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) in business has introduced profound opportunities for improving decision-making, efficiency, and profitability. Traditionally, the purpose of business has often been framed through the lens of maximizing shareholder value (MSV), a concept popularized by Milton Friedman and further developed by Jensen and Meckling. While AI and ML can enhance shareholder returns by enabling precise forecasting, automated decision-making, and optimization of operations, reliance on MSV as the sole objective introduces significant ethical, strategic, and societal risks. This paper examines the limitations of pursuing MSV in AIdriven business contexts, focusing on short-termism, stakeholder neglect, reputational risks, and ethical dilemmas. Through practical scenarios drawn from financial services, retail, and human resource management, the analysis highlights how AI/ML, if unmoderated, can amplify the inherent shortcomings of MSV. Additionally, the paper identifies gaps in current research, noting that existing studies have rarely integrated discussions of AI ethics with the classical MSV debate. By providing a conceptual framework that links AI-driven analytics to stakeholder-inclusive approaches, this study contributes to a more responsible understanding of value creation in contemporary business environments. Recommendations are offered for integrating ethical AI practices, multi-metric performance evaluation, and long-term strategic planning to balance shareholder and stakeholder interests.

detail.abstract: Aim/purpose-The rapid convergence of human cognition and artificial intelligence (AI) is redefining the essence of leadership across industries. This study aims to conceptualize and empirically validate a novel leadership paradigm-the Human-AI Collective Leadership (HAIL) framework-grounded in ethical, cognitive, and adaptive integration between humans and intelligent systems. The purpose of the research is to construct a theoretically robust and practically applicable model that guides leaders in navigating complex, data-driven ecosystems with integrity, agility, and inclusivity. Employing a multidisciplinary synthesis of literature from behavioral science, AI ethics, and organizational leadership, the study develops HAIL as a hybrid governance framework comprising four interlinked dimensions: ethical stewardship, cognitive symbiosis, distributed collaboration, and evolutionary learning. The framework was evaluated through comparative analysis and applied validation in healthcare, corporate, and public-sector contexts. Findings demonstrate that organizations adopting HAIL exhibit enhanced decision precision, stakeholder trust, and systemic adaptability. The research contributes to leadership theory by extending adaptive and ethical leadership constructs into the digital domain, offering a replicable model for responsible and intelligent organizational transformation. Ultimately, this paper argues that the future of leadership lies in harnessing collective intelligence through human-AI collaboration. By adopting the HAIL model, leaders can unlock new forms of organizational capability, ensuring that AI-enabled leadership is not only technologically sophisticated but also ethically grounded, participatory, and authentically human.

detail.abstract: This study examines the ethical and governance challenges posed by algorithmic bias in artificial intelligence (AI), emphasizing its implications for fairness, accountability, and transparency. As AI systems increasingly influence decisions across sectors such as healthcare, finance, human resources, and criminal justice, biased data and flawed model design can perpetuate systemic inequalities and discrimination. Drawing from recent literature, the paper explores how biases originate from sampling errors, incomplete data, and non-representative training sets, leading to unfair outcomes that undermine trust and ethical responsibility. Case studies—including biased medical diagnostics, facial recognition disparities, and the COMPAS recidivism tool—illustrate the real-world consequences of unchecked AI bias. The analysis highlights the need for transparent, auditable, and ethically guided AI frameworks supported by interdisciplinary collaboration among technologists, policymakers, and ethicists. Ultimately, this paper argues that mitigating algorithmic bias is not only a technical necessity but also a moral imperative to ensure that AI systems advance social justice, protect individual rights, and foster public trust in technology-driven governance.

title: Cost Shocks and Production Reorganization: Evidence from the Goods and Services Tax Reform in India
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) - CUHK Business School, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) - CUHK Business School and The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK)

detail.title: Cost Shocks and Production Reorganization: Evidence from the Goods and Services Tax Reform in India
detail.abstract: Manufacturing firms routinely face large exogenous cost shocks that fundamentally alter their cost structures. Examples of these shocks include new carbon pricing policies, tariffs, supply chain disruptions, and tax reforms. When such shocks occur, firms confront a critical operational dilemma: should they reorganize their product portfolios and production processes to minimize costs, or maintain operational continuity to preserve efficiency? This paper investigates this cost-efficiency trade-off using India's 2017 Goods and Services Tax (GST) reform as a large-scale natural experiment. Leveraging granular plant-level data on 72,000 manufacturing facilities over nine years, we construct plant-specific measures of effective tax changes that account for both output tax-rate changes and the elimination of cascading input taxes. We find that plants facing larger tax increases systematically shift toward lower-rate product categories and away from high-rate ones. We distinguish between two adjustment strategies: reclassification-minor product modifications that preserve existing production capabilities, and reorganization-fundamental operational restructuring requiring new input portfolios. Resource-constrained plants predominantly rely on low-cost reclassification, while larger, capital-intensive plants undertake deeper reorganization. These adjustments carry significant efficiency consequences. Plants facing larger tax increases experience declines in total factor productivity of approximately 2.2 percent for every 10 percentage-point increase in tax rates. This occurs despite improvements in labor and capital productivity because plants exhibit sharp declines in material productivity. We trace this pattern to systematic shifts toward lower-quality domestic inputs: plants substitute away from imported materials, requiring more units per unit of output. Plants also improve inventory productivity, particularly for work-in-process and finished goods, by tightening working-capital management. Taken together, these patterns reveal a clear cost-efficiency trade-off: plants lower their effective tax and working-capital burdens through portfolio shifts, input substitution, and leaner inventories, but accept lower production efficiency in return. Our findings provide actionable insights for managers building operational resilience and policymakers designing reforms that should account for heterogeneous firm responses and unintended consequences for efficiency and productivity.

title: Visibility and Retail Demand: Evidence from Bike Share
affiliations: University of Toronto, Toronto, Canada and University of Toronto - Rotman School of Management

detail.title: Visibility and Retail Demand: Evidence from Bike Share
detail.abstract: Storefronts are central to how retailers convert passerby traffic into customers, yet rigorous evidence on role of a storefront remains limited. Instead, retail models tend to emphasize proximity to consumers as a predictor of retail traffic and sales. We examine the role of storefront visibility, rather than location per se, in driving retail traffic by linking the staggered expansion of shared bike networks in New York City and Boston with high-frequency cellphone mobility data on more than 1000 retailers. New bike share stations create a plausibly exogenous surge in passerby traffic. Using exact bike share station locations, we measure line-of-sight observability between stations and storefronts. Our results show that only visible retailers experience significant gains in store visits after the opening of a bike share station. Storefront features like informative signage and legible fonts further amplify these effects. These findings highlight the marketing communications role of storefront visibility.

title: Beyond Asimov: The Moral Covenant for Artificial Intelligence A Universal Manifesto for Embedding Ethics in Machines

detail.title: Beyond Asimov: The Moral Covenant for Artificial Intelligence A Universal Manifesto for Embedding Ethics in Machines
detail.abstract:
Humanity stands at the edge of a moral frontier. For the first time, we are not merely building tools; we are shaping minds that shape us. Beyond Asimov: The Moral Covenant for Artificial Intelligence calls for the restoration of moral gravity in an age where power has outpaced conscience.

Beyond Asimov: The Moral Covenant for Artificial Intelligence draws from the enduring wisdom of the world’s great moral civilizations: the covenantal law of the Hebrews, the compassion of Christ, the cultivated virtue of Confucius, and the disciplined stewardship of Islam.

This Manifesto unites their common truths into a universal ethical architecture for intelligent life. It argues that AI must not be governed by fear of harm but guided by reverence for life, truth, and human dignity. The work proposes ten foundational laws through which intelligence, human or artificial, may remain corrigible, transparent, and compassionate.

More than a code of control, it is a constitution of conscience and a call to re-anchor creation in accountability so that what we build does not extinguish what makes us human.

title: Behavioral Finance and Investor Decision Dynamics in Uncertain Markets

detail.title: Behavioral Finance and Investor Decision Dynamics in Uncertain Markets
detail.abstract:
This Study examines investor decision dynamics in contexts of heightened market uncertainty, drawing on behavioural finance theory and empirical evidence. It addresses the following research questions:

(1) How do cognitive biases and emotional factors influence investor responses in uncertain markets?

(2) What are the decision pathways and heuristics that investors adopt when traditional models fail?

(3) What implications arise for market efficiency, financial advising, and investor education?

The study combines a systematic literature review, in‐depth investor interviews/case studies, and quantitative analysis of investor behaviour across select uncertain market episodes. The findings reveal significant divergences from normative decision models: investors persist in heuristics under uncertainty, amplify risk perceptions, and adapt decision heuristics dynamically.

The book argues that understanding these decision dynamics is vital for financial institutions, advisors, and policy makers aiming to mitigate mispricing, investor vulnerability, and behavioural market inefficiencies.

The contributions are threefold:

(1) a conceptual framework linking investor decision pathways to market uncertainty regimes.

(2) empirical evidence of behavioural heuristics in uncertain environments.

(3) practical implications for investor education and risk‐management practice.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the claim that customer-owned banks offer more favourable rates for deposits and loans than shareholder-owned banks. The empirical analysis based on data extracted from the financial statements of 66 Authorised Deposit-Taking Institutions (ADIs) in Australia does not support this claim. Customer-owned ADIs (COIs) report higher Net Interest Margins (NIMs) and thus offer less favourable rates than shareholder-owned ADIs. In addition, customer-owned banks have lower profitability. detail.abstract: Knowledge spillovers are a common rationale for government support of innovation, yet evidence on their magnitude remains limited. In this paper, I quantify the wedge that spillovers create between social and private rates of return to innovation. To do so, I build a novel semi-endogenous growth model featuring multiproduct firms and endogenous exit of products. In equilibrium, product exit exhibits negative selection and is preceded by a gradual decline in market share, consistent with facts I document using barcode-level data. Through the lens of the model, these dynamics of product exit are informative about spillovers: by accelerating growth in the quality of new products, stronger spillovers increase the rate at which incumbent products lose market share and exit. Since comprehensive datasets track firms rather than products, I leverage the model to infer the wedge created by spillovers from data on firm exit by age. Across U.S. private nonfarm employer businesses, I infer spillovers that drive a 16 percentage point wedge between the social and private rates of return to innovation.

detail.abstract:
The assumption of going concern lies at the heart of auditing and assurance, anchoring the valuation of assets, classification of liabilities, and reliability of financial statements. Yet assessing whether an entity can continue operating remains one of the most judgment-intensive and uncertain aspects of audit practice. Traditional approaches rely heavily on auditors’ professional judgment, experience, and qualitative interpretation of financial and nonfinancial signals. While indispensable, these human-centered methods are vulnerable to subjectivity, inconsistency, and hindsight bias, particularly during periods of economic volatility.

This paper explores how artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping the auditor’s approach to going concern assessment by transforming a largely judgment-based process into one informed by data-driven prediction. Through the integration of machine learning, predictive analytics, and natural language processing, AI systems can synthesize vast quantities of financial and contextual data to identify early warning signs of distress, enhance predictive accuracy, and promote greater consistency across engagements. Evidence from recent demonstrates that AI models outperform traditional ratio analysis in forecasting financial distress and supporting auditors’ evaluation of business viability.

However, the infusion of AI into audit judgment also raises profound ethical, methodological, and regulatory challenges. Concerns about transparency, data bias, explainability, and accountability underscore the need for careful governance and evolving professional standards. The paper argues that the optimal path forward is not the replacement of human auditors by intelligent systems but their collaboration—where algorithmic precision complements human skepticism, ethical reasoning, and contextual awareness.

Ultimately, this study positions AI not as a threat to auditor judgment but as its most promising ally. By merging computational foresight with professional discernment, the auditing profession can transform going concern evaluation from a retrospective exercise into a forward-looking, continuously adaptive safeguard of financial integrity and public trust.

title: The Unitary Executive and the Due Process State
affiliations: Notre Dame Law School and Yale University - Law School

detail.title: The Unitary Executive and the Due Process State
detail.abstract: In Trump v. Slaughter, the Supreme Court will consider whether to overrule Humphrey's Executor v. United States, 295 U.S. 602 (1935), a landmark case that affirmed Congress's authority to limit the President's ability to fire members of the Federal Trade Commission (FTC). Proponents argue that this is necessary to ensure unitary executive control over the significant policymaking functions of the FTC and other historically independent administrative agencies. But the legal principles reflected in Humphrey's Executor are also the foundation upon which Congress has constructed what we call the "due process state," i.e., the many impartial officers and institutions that the President requires to discharge his Article II duty to ensure the faithful execution of adjudicatory statutes. This essay argues that the unitary executive and the due process state can-and indeed must-coexist.

title: Beyond A/B Testing: Estimating Heterogeneous Treatment Effects in Digital Marketing Using Causal Machine Learning

detail.title: Beyond A/B Testing: Estimating Heterogeneous Treatment Effects in Digital Marketing Using Causal Machine Learning
detail.abstract: The digital marketing paradigm is undergoing a fundamental transformation, shifting from aggregate optimization based on Average Treatment Effects (ATE) to granular, personalized intervention strategies driven by the estimation of Heterogeneous Treatment Effects (HTE). While the Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT)-manifested industrially as A/B testing-remains the gold standard for causal identification, its reliance on mean effects obscures critical variability in consumer behavior, failing to distinguish between "Persuadables," "Sure Things," and value-destroying "Sleeping Dogs". This research paper proposes a rigorous comparative analysis of Causal Machine Learning (CML) methodologies designed to estimate the Conditional Average Treatment Effect (CATE). We propose to systematically evaluate three distinct estimator classesthe S-Learner, the T-Learner, and the Honest Causal Forest-utilizing two premier industry benchmark datasets: the Hillstrom MineThatData Email Analytics dataset and the Criteo Uplift Prediction dataset. Our theoretical synthesis suggests that while the S-Learner provides a low-variance baseline suitable for weak-signal environments, we hypothesize it will systematically underestimate treatment heterogeneity due to regularization bias. Conversely, we anticipate the T-Learner will offer asymptotic unbiasedness but suffer from significant variance in sample-fragmented regimes. We expect the Causal Forest, particularly when implemented with "honest splitting," to emerge as the superior estimator for high-dimensional marketing data, offering a robust mechanism to maximize incremental Return on Ad Spend (ROAS) while strictly controlling for the risk of negative uplift.

title: Executive Learning as a System Property: Why Organizational Adaptation Requires More than Individual Leadership Development
affiliations: Helptext Consulting

detail.title: Executive Learning as a System Property: Why Organizational Adaptation Requires More than Individual Leadership Development
detail.abstract: Organizations today operate in environments characterized by volatility, complexity, and accelerating technological change. Under these conditions, executive and board-level learning is no longer a developmental option; it is a structural requirement for strategic adaptation and organizational resilience. Yet research across leadership, governance, and digital transformation reveals a persistent executive learning gap: leaders' mental models and learning practices evolve more slowly than the environments they must navigate. This gap produces predictable organizational failures, including strategic inertia, brittle systems, cultural strain, and ineffective technology adoption. This paper synthesizes research on adaptive leadership, systems thinking, upper-echelons theory, organizational learning, and executive cognition to conceptualize leadership learning as a system-level property, shaped by governance structures, decision architectures, information flows, and feedback loops. It integrates insights from the literature on emotional, organizational, and technical debt to demonstrate how learning failures accumulate and reinforce one another through systemic loops. An integrative framework is presented that outlines the inputs, learning architecture, and reinforcing loops that determine whether organizations learn, stagnate, or decay. The paper concludes with implications for executives, boards, regulators, and HR/L&D leaders, emphasizing governance design, boundary clarity, reflective practice, and continuous sensemaking as core mechanisms for embedding learning into the organizational system. Executive learning, the paper argues, is not merely an individual competency but a structural capability essential for resilience in complex environments.

title: EFFECT OF FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENT ON CAPITAL MARKET DEVELOPMENT IN THE MINT ECONOMIES: A REFLECTION OF COMPLEMENTARITY OR SUBSTITUTABILITY HYPOTHESIS?
affiliations: Modibbo Adama University of Technology - Department of Banking and Finance

detail.title: EFFECT OF FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENT ON CAPITAL MARKET DEVELOPMENT IN THE MINT ECONOMIES: A REFLECTION OF COMPLEMENTARITY OR SUBSTITUTABILITY HYPOTHESIS?
detail.abstract: The four countries, Mexico, Indonesia, Nigeria and Turkey, popularly called the MINT economies, have been regarded as another group of developing countries that have the advantageous positions, geographically, economically and demographically to influence the world growth in a substantial manner. These countries have attracted foreign direct investments (FDI), which are expected to affect their financial markets in general and the capital market but the effect could be positive (complementarity hypothesis) or negative (substitutability hypothesis). Since the health of an economy is often gauged by its capital market, this study therefore while testing the hypotheses, investigated the effect of foreign direct investment on capital market development in the MINT economies, during the period, 1993-2023. The quantitative data used in the study which were obtained from the World Development Indicators, were analysed using Panel-Autoregressive Distributed Lag (P-ARDL) technique. The study found the existence of a long-run, positive and significant impact of FDI on capital market development. However, in the short-run, FDI was found to exert negative and significant impact on capital market development in the MINTs. Specifically, in the short-run, FDI had a negative and non-significant impact on capital market development in Mexico, Turkey and Indonesia, but there was a negative and significant effect of FDI on capital market development in Nigeria. The study concludes that FDI inflow is a promoter of capital market development in the MINT economies. It is therefore recommended that policies, principles, strategies and programmes that will stimulate the inflow of foreign direct investment to the MINT countries, should be embarked upon/intensified by the governments. Also, some shock absolvers should be put in place in the MINTs, particularly in Nigeria, to cushion the short-run, negative impact of FDI on capital market development.

title: A Novel Safety-Constrained Reinforcement Learning State Control Strategy for Pipeline Inspection Gauges
affiliations: Northeastern University (USA),  and

detail.title: A Novel Safety-Constrained Reinforcement Learning State Control Strategy for Pipeline Inspection Gauges
detail.abstract: Under high-dimensional state spaces with complex dynamic friction characteristics and under non-stationary operating conditions, the velocity control of self-propelled Pipeline Inspection Gauges is highly susceptible to multiple disturbances, making it difficult to maintain stability and robustness. This study presents a deep reinforcement learning control strategy that integrates safety constraints with strong generalization capability. The proposed method incorporates distributed action-value estimation and a robust loss function to improve uncertainty modeling and suppress gradient explosion, embeds an intrinsic reward mechanism to enhance exploration efficiency, and applies a policy update magnitude constraint to satisfy stringent safety requirements in industrial applications. The proposed algorithm is trained in the high-fidelity simulation environment and bench marked against multiple reinforcement learning approaches, yielding a 2.75%–12.14% increase in cumulative rewards and a 33%–73.8% reduction in error fluctuation. The learned policy is subsequently deployed on a physical platform and validated under a variety of operating conditions. Experimental results reveal that the proposed method reduces the interquartile range of speed fluctuations by more than 7.7% and the mean absolute error by more than 29.9%, thereby demonstrating excellent robustness, adaptability, and suitability for deployment in complex environments. These findings provide both a theoretical foundation and practical guidance for intelligent pipeline inspection control tasks, as well as for the safe and reliable deployment of deep reinforcement learning in complex industrial settings.

detail.abstract: This study examines the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into internal auditing, highlighting its potential to improve efficiency, independence, and the overall quality of audit processes. AI enhances audit functions through automation, real-time data analysis, and improved cybersecurity, enabling auditors to focus on higher-value activities and deliver more reliable financial reporting. However, the adoption of AI also introduces challenges such as algorithmic bias, cybersecurity risks, competence gaps, and the loss of human professional skepticism. Despite these limitations, research shows that when implemented responsibly, AI significantly strengthens internal audit quality and organizational governance. The paper concludes by recommending that firms combine human oversight with AI technologies to maximize benefits while maintaining ethical and professional standards.

detail.abstract: People frequently compete with one another for awards, benefits, contracts, positions, or roles. One of the regulatory challenges in these contexts lies in preventing people from making dishonest claims to win such competitions. Honesty pledges, asking people to commit to ethical behavior ex-ante, have been found to reduce cheating under noncompetitive settings (when rewards were given based on individual reports only). However, as people behave differently under competitive settings, it is unclear whether honesty pledges could be effective and recommended in such situations as well. In four experiments, we apply honesty pledges to competitive and non-competitive settings, finding that pledges remain effective in reducing cheating behavior under competitive contexts (Studies 1-4). Moreover, this effect is not crowded out if a sanction (fine) is added to the honesty pledge (Study 2). Honesty pledges are also effective among people who tend to cheat more, due to low or overestimated task-related ability (Study 2) or due to high competitiveness (Study 3). Additionally, people's estimations regarding others' cheating behavior explain why pledges accompanied by descriptive honesty norms affect cheating behavior (Study 3). Lastly, even in high-stakes competitive environments that demonstrably increased dishonesty, honesty pledges remained effective in reducing dishonesty (Study 4). These findings demonstrate that honesty pledges can serve as effective non-coercive regulatory instruments to reduce dishonesty in competitive environments, offering advantages over traditional enforcement mechanisms while remaining effective even among individuals most prone to cheating and under high-stakes conditions, with important implications for organizational policy design and regulatory approaches.

detail.title: Machine Vision-Based Metal Workpiece Surface Defect Detection System
detail.abstract: A metal surface defect detection system that integrates perception guided preprocessing and improved deep learning is proposed to address the diverse shapes and sizes of metal surface defects, which are highly susceptible to noise interference and difficult to achieve high-precision detection standards using existing methods. Firstly, based on the perception of noise characteristics, adaptive hybrid filtering is used to suppress noise, and guided filtering is employed for edge optimization; Adopting the fusion multi-scale gradient adaptive Canny algorithm to accurately extract defect contours. On this basis, the preprocessed and enhanced high-quality images are input into an improved ResNet18 deep network for feature learning and classification. The improved ResNet18 model reconstructs a dedicated classification layer for six typical metal defects, combined with global average pooling, significantly reducing the number of parameters while enhancing the model's generalization ability. The experimental results show that the final detection accuracy of this model is as high as 99.74%, which is 23.8% higher than the baseline model, fully verifying its effectiveness, robustness, and practical value in complex working conditions.

detail.abstract:
This paper presents a comprehensive framework for developing financial technology specifically designed for neurodivergent populations, with particular focus on adults with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). Despite representing 4.4% of the U.S. adult population (11+ million individuals), people with ADHD face unique financial management challenges that existing fintech applications fail to address. Current personal finance platforms require sustained attention, linear thinking, and executive function capabilities that are characteristically impaired in ADHD, creating a significant market gap.
We propose SnapWealth, a mobile financial companion application employing dopamine-optimized interface design, impulse control technology, voice-first interaction, and AI-powered behavioral pattern recognition specifically calibrated for ADHD cognitive patterns. The platform integrates banking APIs (Plaid), artificial intelligence (OpenAI GPT-4), and behavioral psychology principles to create the first financial management system designed from inception for neurodivergent users rather than adapted from neurotypical frameworks.
Market analysis demonstrates substantial opportunity: 11 million U.S. adults with ADHD, zero direct competitors with ADHD-specific design, and strong unit economics with lifetime value to customer acquisition cost ratio of 4.77:1. Conservative financial projections estimate $960,000 annual recurring revenue in Year 1 (10,000 users) scaling to $48 million by Year 5 (500,000 users), with break-even achieved at 18-20 months.
Technical implementation employs React Native for cross-platform mobile development, Node.js microservices architecture, PostgreSQL database with ADHD-specific schema extensions, and proprietary machine learning algorithms for impulse purchase detection (0.7+ confidence threshold) and medication correlation analysis. The three-tier subscription model (Free, Premium $9.99/month, Expert $29.99/month) generates diversified revenue while maintaining accessibility for lower-income users.
This research contributes to emerging literature on inclusive fintech design, neurodiversity in technology development, and behavioral economics applications in personal finance. The SnapWealth framework offers a replicable model for addressing underserved populations through targeted technology design that works with rather than against cognitive differences. Findings have implications for fintech product development, venture capital investment in neurodiversity-focused technologies, and public policy regarding financial inclusion for disabled populations.
